when: between 2:20 and 2:55, before the first crabs spawn
asks: do I gank before crab
crab or gank mid first
clear's done, crab isn't up yet
got a few seconds before scuttle, gank?
say: Gank mid on your way to the crab, before it spawns; a burned Flash pays later, or walk straight to crab if their mid's hugging tower.
more: The seconds before the crabs spawn are dead time anyway. A gank that starts on the walk to river costs you nothing you were going to farm.
Their jungler is usually still finishing camps then, so there is rarely a counter-gank. Even if all you get is Flash, mid is open again once you hit level 6.
If you'd have to wait around for the wave, skip it. Being first at the crab with your mid moving is worth more than a slow gank.
check: Is their mid laner past the middle of the lane, and did you see their jungler on the other side?
breaks: Wrong if their mid is under tower or their jungler is already at that crab: go to the other crab or your next camp instead.
basis: pro:Gank on the walk to the crab

when: before 1:30 and your bot lane has an early lane bully
asks: my bot lane is strong early, where do I start
we have a Draven lane, how do I path
should I path bot for my lane bully
which side do I clear toward
say: Clear toward bot so their jungler can't visit that lane for free, or mirror him on the far side if your bot can't push.
more: A strong early duo wins the two-on-two by itself. Your job is to make sure it stays a two-on-two, by being the jungler standing on that side.
The map splits: you own the bot half, he owns the top half. Your top laner has to play safe for a few minutes and should be told.
The payoff comes around the first dragon. A bot lane that has pushed for five minutes gives you that dragon without a fight.
check: Is your bot lane actually pushing the wave, and does your top laner know he is alone?
breaks: Wrong if your bot lane lost the first trades and is stuck under tower: then path away from it and play for your top side instead.
basis: pro:Split the map for a lane bully

when: the enemy jungler died before 2:30
asks: killed their jungler at his buff, now what
got first blood on their jungler, do I take his buff
their jungler's dead level one, what do I take
I won the invade, stay or leave
say: Take his nearest small camps for the fast level, then leave; or take the buff first if your laners are already walking over.
more: He respawns quickly this early, so you have time for one or two camps, not his whole side. Small camps next to you are the quickest experience.
The point is the level lead. You reach your next level first and he comes back to a half-empty jungle with nowhere good to start.
Your own camps are still up behind you. Go back to them straight after, so you end the clear ahead rather than even.
check: Which of his camps are still alive, and are his laners walking toward you?
breaks: Wrong if his mid or bot lane is already on the way with push: take one camp at most and get out through your own side.
basis: pro:Level one pick on the jungler

when: before 1:30
asks: should I go mess with their jungler level one
do I invade with my jungler at the start
can I delay their jungler's clear
worth leaving lane to bother their jungle
say: You can stand on his first camp and drag it out to slow his clear, or stay in lane if your carry can't hold the wave.
more: A jungler who finishes a camp late is late to everything after it: the crab, the first gank, level 4. That delay helps all three of your lanes.
You pay with your own experience. You reach level 2 late, so your lane has to give up the early push while you are gone.
It works best with a tanky or slippery support and a carry who can farm safely under pressure for a minute.
check: Where did their jungler start, and can your carry last-hit alone without being zoned off the wave?
breaks: Wrong if their lane is the one that wins early trades: your carry gets pushed off the wave and you both fall behind. Stay and fight for level 2 instead.
basis: pro:Support delays the first clear

when: you are level 6 and their jungler is level 5
asks: I'm six before their jungler, what do I do
got my ult first, where do I use it
I hit six, gank or invade
level lead on their jungler, how do I use it
say: Use the ult now on a lane that's missing Flash, before he catches up; or walk into his jungle and fight him if no lane's reachable.
more: An ultimate he doesn't have yet is the biggest gap you will hold over him all game. It lasts about one clear, so farming through it wastes it.
A laner without Flash can't answer an ultimate gank. A kill there right before a dragon or the grubs usually means you take that objective too.
If lanes are all pushed into their towers, finding him at his camps works as well. He can't win the duel a level down.
check: Which enemy laners used Flash recently, and which of his camps are about to respawn?
breaks: Wrong if their mid is level 6 with push and yours is not: he arrives first to any fight in the jungle. Gank a side lane instead.
basis: pro:Ultimate before the other jungler

when: you are level 5 and their mid or jungler is level 6
asks: can I invade right now
should I steal his camps
I'm five, is it safe in their jungle
want to take his buff, good idea?
say: Stay out of his jungle until you're 6; take your own camps for the level, or invade only if their mid is stuck under tower.
more: One level sounds small, but level 6 is an ultimate. Walking into their side a level down means a single catch is a death, not a trade.
It usually costs more than the kill. They take your Flash or your life, then a camp of yours, then the next objective while you walk back.
One more camp is often all you need. Finish it, then the same invade is an even fight.
check: How close are you to level 6, and is their mid laner pushed up or shoved in?
breaks: Wrong if you can see both their mid and jungler on the far side of the map: then the camp is free, take it quickly.
basis: pro:Invading a level down

when: no dragon, grubs or herald spawns in the next two minutes
asks: nothing's up, what do I do
no objectives for a while, where do I go
dead time, farm or gank
what now, everything's on cooldown
say: Full clear and recall so your item's finished before the next spawn, or sit on a lane for plates if your camps are down.
more: Quiet minutes are when item leads are made. The jungler who walks into the next objective with a finished item decides how that fight goes.
Plan it backwards from the spawn: clear, recall, and be walking to the pit with about half a minute to spare.
If your camps are gone, helping a lane shove and take plates is real gold, and it pushes that wave for the objective after.
check: Which of your camps are up, and how much gold are you short of your next item?
breaks: Wrong if an enemy laner has no Flash and is pushed up: that kill is worth more than a quiet clear. Gank first, then reset.
basis: pro:Use dead time for items

when: you ganked a lane in the last three minutes and got no kill
asks: I burned his Flash, when do I go back
they flashed, do I gank again
who do I gank next
should I repeat the gank mid
say: Go back to that lane within the next couple of clears while his Flash is down, or take camps if the wave's under his tower.
more: A burned Flash is only worth something if somebody uses it. It comes back after a few minutes, so the return visit has a deadline.
Champions who lean on Flash to escape, like immobile mages and marksmen, are close to free kills in that window, more so once you have an ultimate.
Tell the laner. If he keeps the wave on his side for one wave, the second gank is much shorter.
check: Did you actually see the Flash, how long ago, and where is that wave now?
breaks: Wrong if the laner has a dash that takes him to his tower anyway: the Flash mattered less than you think. Pick a different lane.
basis: pro:Return to the lane without Flash

when: your team killed the herald and you are holding it
asks: where do I use herald
which lane for herald
do I drop herald mid
when do I use the herald
say: Drop it in a lane with your wave already there and their jungler seen elsewhere, or hold it if they're waiting to kill it.
more: A herald that dies before it charges gave you nothing. The teams that lose it usually dropped it into three defenders with crowd control ready.
A wave in front of it and a missing enemy jungler are the two things that let it reach the tower.
A side lane with a low tower is fine. The first tower opens that side of the map for the next objective.
check: Is your wave at their tower, and can you see their jungler and the laner who would defend?
breaks: Wrong if a dragon spawns in under a minute and you can't be in both places: drop it mid right before the spawn as a distraction instead.
basis: pro:A herald needs a wave and an empty lane

when: before 1:45 and the enemy support is an engage champion
asks: where do I ward level one
they have Leona, how do I start the lane
should I ward the lane bush
how do I stop the bush cheese
say: Ward the lane brush before minions arrive so their engage support can't hide in it, or hold the brush yourself if you're the stronger lane.
more: An engage support wants to stand unseen in the brush and jump whoever walks up for the first minions. A ward there takes that away.
Seen in the open, he has to walk at you through your ranged attacks. That often costs him half his health before level 2.
It also decides the race to level 2. The side that can hit minions freely gets there first and the other has to back off.
check: Is their support missing from lane as the wave arrives, and did your carry ward the other brush?
breaks: Wrong if you need that ward for the river because their jungler ganks early: keep it and stand back from the brush instead.
basis: pro:Brush wards against engage supports

when: you are an engage support and the enemy bot lane is ranged with an enchanter
asks: can I go in on them
do I engage here
should I all in bot
I keep losing trades when I engage
say: Go in only if you'd win the walk back out too; at low health hold the wave near your tower, or wait for your jungler.
more: Landing the engage is half the trade. Against slows and a polymorph or shield, the damage you take walking away is often more than you dealt.
Health is what makes you a threat. A low engage support can't go in, and both of you become a dive target.
Staying healthy under tower loses a few minions but keeps the lane playable until level 6 or a gank changes it.
check: How much health do you and your carry have, and are their slow and their peel ability available?
breaks: Wrong if their carry has just used his escape or summoner spell: then the exit is safe and you should go in at once.
basis: pro:Plan the exit of the trade

when: before 14:00 and a dragon is up or spawns within two minutes
asks: should I roam mid
where do I go after we shove
can I leave lane for a bit
how do I help mid as support
say: Clear the river brush with a control ward and wait in it with your jungler for mid to step up, or stay if your carry's low.
more: A control ward in the river beside mid turns that path into a lane you can use again and again. They never know whether someone is standing there.
The catch is usually whoever walks into the dark river first, often their jungler coming to help. A dead jungler next to the dragon means the dragon.
Leave after one wave if nothing happens. Your carry is alone and loses minions for every wave you are away.
check: Is the river brush free of enemy wards, and can your carry farm safely alone?
breaks: Wrong if their bot lane is stronger and can dive your carry while you're gone: ward the river and walk back instead.
basis: pro:Brush wait beside mid

when: a dragon or baron spawns in about a minute and a half
asks: I'm out of wards, what do I do
should I back before dragon
when do I recall for wards
how do I set up vision for the objective
say: Recall now and come back with full wards before the spawn, or stay only if your team already holds the river.
more: A support with no wards at the spawn is a body, not vision. The other team sees that and walks into your jungle the moment you leave.
Recalling early is the fix. You return as the fight forms, with control wards, and your team isn't guessing which brush is safe.
Tell your team you're gone for those seconds so nobody starts a fight four against five.
check: How many wards and control wards do you hold, and how long until the spawn?
breaks: Wrong if the spawn is under half a minute away: you won't be back in time. Stay grouped and use what you have.
basis: pro:Reset for wards before the spawn

when: you died in the last two minutes while away from your team
asks: I keep dying when I ward
how do I ward without getting caught
is it safe to go ward
they keep catching me in the jungle
say: Ward only right after your nearest wave is pushed and with someone beside you, or ward your own jungle entrances if you're behind.
more: Supports die warding because they go when it suits them, not when the map allows it. A pushed wave means the enemy is busy and your team can follow.
Each solo death before an objective costs more than the ward was worth: your team loses its engage or its peel for that fight.
When behind, the right ward line is closer to home. Seeing them enter your jungle is enough to keep your carries alive.
check: Is the wave nearest to you pushed, who is walking with you, and how many enemies show on the map?
breaks: Wrong if their whole team just showed on the far side: then go deep alone and quickly, that window is safe.
basis: pro:Supports die warding alone

when: a dragon or baron is up or spawns within a minute
asks: where do I stand in the fight
who do I peel
where should I be at dragon
do I stay with the carry or go front
say: Stand on the side their flanker would come from, between him and your carry; or step forward to engage if nobody's missing.
more: Dive champions want the angle your carry can't see: behind the pit or through the side brush. One body standing there closes it.
You don't have to kill the flanker. If he has to walk through you, your carries get the seconds they need to keep hitting the front line.
It looks passive, but fights against dive are won by the carries staying alive, not by the first engage.
check: Which enemy is missing from the front, and which entrance to the pit is unwarded?
breaks: Wrong if their threats are all in front of you: then there's no flank to guard, and your crowd control belongs on whoever walks up first.
basis: pro:Guard the flank behind the pit

when: after 14:00 and your ultimate is an area crowd control or a big save
asks: do I ult here
when do I use my ult
should I add my ult to the kill
do I save my ultimate
say: If he's dying anyway, hold your ult for whoever comes to save him; or use it now if he might get away.
more: Once a target is locked down, more crowd control on him adds nothing. The fight is decided by the second wave: his teammates arriving.
An area ultimate held on that angle makes them choose between watching him die and walking into it.
Thrown on a dead man, it leaves your team with nothing when they turn on you a moment later.
check: Is the target locked down with no Flash, and which enemies are close enough to arrive?
breaks: Wrong if he has a stasis item or Flash and your ult is what keeps him in place: use it straight away.
basis: pro:Hold the ult for the rescuers

when: no dragon, herald or baron spawns in the next two minutes
asks: is it worth going in if I die
should I just engage
can I trade myself for their Flash
do I go for the pick
say: Trading yourself for their carry's Flash is fine only if your team can jump him before it's back; otherwise keep your life and keep warding.
more: With nothing on the map for them to take, your death costs little. A carry without Flash, though, is a target for the next few minutes.
The trade is only good if it's cashed. Someone has to go at that carry again, ideally right before the next objective.
If your team isn't the kind that follows up, you gave a kill for a cooldown nobody used.
check: What spawns next and when, and does your team have a way onto that carry?
breaks: Wrong if an objective is about to spawn or your own carry is nearby without help: your death then hands them the fight.
basis: pro:A death for a Flash must be cashed

when: before 14:00 and two or more of you are in the same lane
asks: who tanks the tower
how do we dive him
do I go in first
can we dive this
say: Decide who takes the tower first, and that player leaves early while the second finishes; or wait a wave if nobody's healthy enough.
more: Dives fail when the first player in stays too long. He takes the tower's shots, uses Flash late and dies with the target still alive.
The tanky or full-health player goes first and walks out as soon as the tower turns to someone else. The damage dealer goes second.
If nobody can afford the first shots, a bigger wave next time does that job for you.
check: Who has the most health, how many minions are under the tower, and does the target still have Flash or a shield?
breaks: Wrong if their jungler or a Teleport can arrive mid-dive: you lose two for one. Shove the wave and take the plate instead.
basis: pro:Hand off the tower's shots

when: the enemy support is level 5 and your mid or jungler is level 6
asks: do we dive bot now
should I come bot with my ult
four man bot?
is this a good time to dive their bot lane
say: Dive bot now, before their support gets his ultimate; or just shove and take plates if their mid can follow you down.
more: Supports reach level 6 last. In that gap your side brings an ultimate or two and theirs has none to stop it.
Bring three or four so it's over quickly. A fast dive leaves you standing by the dragon with their bot lane dead.
You pay with a mid wave and maybe a top plate. That's a fair price if two die and the dragon follows.
check: How close is their support to level 6, how big is your wave, and where is their mid laner?
breaks: Wrong if the enemy laners have Teleport and you can see them walking toward it: then it's an even fight under their tower. Take the dragon instead.
basis: pro:Dive before the support hits six

when: you just reached level 6 on a dive champion and their bot lane is level 5 or lower
asks: should I roam bot at six
can I leave top to help bot
do I use my ult bot
top's quiet, do I go somewhere
say: Push your wave and walk or Teleport bot for the kill on their carry, or stay if your tower would lose more than one plate.
more: A top laner's ultimate arriving bot is something nobody there is watching for. On a carry without Flash it's close to certain.
You are selling part of your own lane for it: a wave, maybe a plate. It's worth it when the kill goes to your carry and the dragon follows.
Recall first if you're holding gold. Arriving with old items and then being stuck bot without Teleport is how the roam costs you the lane.
check: Is your wave pushed, did their carry really use Flash, and do you still have Teleport to get back?
breaks: Wrong if your lane opponent can take your tower while you're gone: then hold the lane and let your jungler make that play.
basis: pro:The top laner sells his lane for bot

when: an ally just got a kill on the far side and you have Teleport
asks: do I tp to that fight
should I teleport bot
they got a kill, do I join
is this a good tp
say: If the play's already won, keep Teleport and take your own wave and plates; or use it only if it turns straight into the objective.
more: Teleporting to a fight that is over gives you an assist at most. Meanwhile your wave dies to your tower and your opponent farms alone.
An open lane is the better deal: you take plates, and you still hold Teleport for the next real fight.
The exception is when your arrival makes the herald or dragon safe to start at once. Then it's a trade worth making.
check: How many enemies are still alive over there, and is there an objective up beside the fight?
breaks: Wrong if your teammates are low and more enemies are walking in: then the fight isn't won, and your Teleport is what saves it.
basis: pro:Don't Teleport to a won fight

when: you have Teleport and an ally in another lane is behind in level
asks: they're diving my bot lane, do I tp
should I teleport to help
bot's getting dived
do I leave lane to save them
say: Teleport in if your ally is still healthy under a standing tower, behind the divers; or stay and take plates if he's already dead.
more: Divers are low, in tower range and out of cooldowns a few seconds in. One fresh champion arriving then often turns two deaths into two kills.
Arrive on their exit path, not on top of your ally. They have to walk through you to leave.
If the ally dies before you land, you've appeared alone in front of three people. Then the right answer was your own lane.
check: How much health does your ally have, how many are diving, and is there a ward or minion to land on behind them?
breaks: Wrong if the tower is already gone or your ally is one hit from dead: you arrive too late. Push your own lane hard instead.
basis: pro:Teleport onto the divers' exit

when: before 14:00 and you are even or ahead of your lane opponent in level
asks: how do I stop him from backing
he wants to recall, what do I do
should I push or hold the wave
how do I punish his reset
say: Leave the last minions alive so his wave never reaches your tower and his recall costs a wave, or shove if you must recall too.
more: A laner can only recall for free when his wave is crashing into your tower. If it's stuck in the middle, every recall costs him a wave.
So he stays in lane low and poor, which is exactly when your jungler's gank works.
It takes patience: last-hit only, and keep the minions on your side of the lane.
check: How many minions are left on each side, and do you see their jungler?
breaks: Wrong if you are the one who needs to recall or an objective is about to spawn: push it in and go.
basis: pro:Hold minions to deny the reset

when: before 8:00, you hold enough gold for an item and have Teleport
asks: one more wave or recall
should I back now
do I stay for the wave
when do I recall top
say: Crash this wave and recall before the grubs so Teleport's free for the fight, or stay if your wave's stuck in the middle.
more: Gold in your pocket does nothing in a fight. One more wave often becomes three, and then the grubs start while you still have old items.
Worse, you spend Teleport just to get back to lane. Now you can't join the fight that happens right after.
A recall on a crashed wave loses almost nothing, and you return with an item for the first objective of the game.
check: How much gold do you have, where is the wave, and how long until 8:00?
breaks: Wrong if recalling now gives up a full wave and a plate: fix the wave first, even if it costs you a few seconds.
basis: pro:Spend before the grubs, keep Teleport

when: a dragon is up, their top laner has Teleport and you are both still top
asks: I can't get to dragon, what do I do
my tp is down and they're fighting bot
how do I help from top
do I walk down or stay
say: Start a fight with their top laner so he can't channel Teleport, or just shove for plates if he could kill you.
more: If you can't reach the fight, the next best thing is making sure he can't either. A Teleport can't be channeled while he's being hit and controlled.
You're spending your health bar to keep the fight below even in numbers. That's a good trade even if you lose the duel slightly.
If he ignores you and walks down, take every plate you can. He's paying for that with his tower.
check: Is his Teleport up, do you have a way to interrupt him, and where is their jungler?
breaks: Wrong if he beats you outright in a duel: you die and he teleports anyway. Hit the tower from range instead.
basis: pro:Pin their top so he can't Teleport

when: after 14:00 and you are the side laner
asks: can I keep pushing
my flash is down, is splitting safe
how far do I push
should I split or group
say: With Flash down, stop at the river and catch waves there until it's back; or group if their team keeps sending two at you.
more: A side laner without Flash is the easiest kill on the map, and the death is rarely just a death. It usually leaves your team a player short at baron.
Catching the wave on your side still pulls someone over to answer it. You keep the pressure without offering the pick.
Once Flash is back, the same push is fine again.
check: Is your Flash up, how many enemies show on the map, and is baron alive?
breaks: Wrong if you can see four of them on the other side: then push as far as you like, Flash or not.
basis: pro:No Flash, no deep split

when: a dragon is up and you are a tank with an engage ultimate
asks: do I ult here
should I engage or stay on dragon
they're coming, what do I do
how do I help us finish dragon
say: Throw your ult to push them back off the pit while the dragon dies, then leave; or keep it if your team wants the full fight.
more: An engage ultimate doesn't have to start a fight. Thrown across the entrance, it buys the seconds your jungler needs to finish.
You may lose the ultimate, or even your life, for the dragon. That's a fair price when your team is weaker in a full fight right now.
The mistake is following it in. If your team is walking away, you walk away too.
check: How low is the dragon, and is your team staying to fight or leaving?
breaks: Wrong if your team is stronger and wants the fight: then save it for a real engage on their carries.
basis: pro:Spend the ult to finish the objective

when: you are the engage champion and your team is ahead or even
asks: when do I engage
do I go in now
I engaged and nobody followed
should I start the fight
say: Engage only when your damage dealers are in range behind you; if they're still in river or on a wave, back up or wait.
more: A good engage with nobody behind it is a pick for the other team. They kill you, then walk at four people.
Fights are lost this way even from ahead. The tank goes on a fine angle while the mid laner is still two screens away.
A few seconds of waiting is cheap. The same engage with both carries beside you wins.
check: Where are your two main damage dealers standing right now?
breaks: Wrong if you catch a lone carry with no Flash: then go at once, your team will follow a pick.
basis: pro:Engage when the damage is in range

when: after 14:00 and you have Teleport
asks: where do I teleport
should I flank with tp
do I tp behind them
how do I join this fight
say: Teleport to the side of the fight where your team can reach you, or behind them only if your team's already going in.
more: A flank lands several seconds after you start it. If your team isn't fighting when you arrive, you're alone behind five people.
Deep flanks have decided games the wrong way: the top laner dies first and the big objective goes with him.
Landing beside your team is less showy, but it always adds a player to the fight.
check: Has your team actually engaged, and is the ward you're landing on still unseen?
breaks: Wrong if their carries are standing far behind their front line with no vision: then the deep flank is the winning play.
basis: pro:A deep flank needs a fight in progress

when: you are ahead of a tank top laner who has not finished an armor or magic resist item
asks: I'm winning lane, what now
how do I use my lead top
I'm ahead of their tank
should I keep fighting him or roam
say: Turn the lead into plates or a dive now, before his first defensive item; or roam with your jungler if he's hugging his tower.
more: An early lead over a tank melts on its own. Once he finishes a defensive item he stops dying to you and starts winning long trades.
So the lead needs to become something permanent first: plates, the tower, a kill for your jungler or the grubs.
If you only out-farm him by a wave, he's ahead by the time team fights start.
check: What defensive items does he have, and is your jungler near enough to dive?
breaks: Wrong if he already has that item finished: stop trading into him, and push side waves so he can't join his team for free.
basis: pro:A lead on a tank expires

when: you are a tank and four or more enemy champions deal mostly physical damage
asks: what do I build
armor or health first
what's my first item into this team
do I need magic resist
say: Go armor first, even before health; one magic damage champion won't spend his spells on you. Or split it if their mage is fed.
more: When nearly all their steady damage is physical, armor makes you a wall for the whole team. Their one mage wants your carries, not you.
It also flips your lane. A bruiser who was beating you early stops winning trades once the armor is finished.
Later on it means they can't dive past you or kill you, and your carries get to stand behind that.
check: Who on their team is actually dealing the damage so far, and is their magic damage champion ahead?
breaks: Wrong if the fed enemy is the mage: buy the magic resist item first and armor second.
basis: pro:Stack armor into an all-physical team

when: you are level 5 and your jungler is level 6 or close to it
asks: I'm almost six, when do we go
should my jungler come now
do I fight at five
when's the gank mid
say: Hold the trade until the wave gives you 6, then go with your jungler at once; or go now if their mid has no Flash.
more: The minion that gives you level 6 is a timer the enemy rarely watches. One second you're level 5, the next you have an ultimate in the middle of a trade.
Have your jungler beside the lane as that wave arrives. A collapse with two fresh ultimates on someone who expected neither is very hard to survive.
If the dragon is up, a kill on mid then is a free dragon straight after.
check: How many minions until you level, and is your jungler close enough to arrive on that wave?
breaks: Wrong if their mid is already 6 and you are low: he gets to use his ultimate first. Farm the level from range.
basis: pro:Collapse on the level six wave

when: before 14:00 and the enemy jungler has no kill or assist in the last minute
asks: which side of lane do I stand
where's the gank coming from
how do I not get ganked mid
is it safe to push
say: Stand on the side of the lane away from where his clear should end, or toward the side you've warded if you don't know.
more: A jungler passing through mid comes from the side he just cleared. Standing on the far side makes his walk long enough for you to leave.
It costs nothing. You farm the same wave from a different spot.
Combine it with one ward on the other side and most ganks have to use Flash just to reach you.
check: Which side did he start on, and which river brush is warded?
breaks: Wrong if he was just seen on a side lane: then stand wherever lets you trade best, the window is open.
basis: pro:Lean away from the jungler's side

when: you have died twice to their mid laner and are behind in CS
asks: I'm 0 and 2, what do I do
I can't lane against him
how do I come back mid
lost lane, now what
say: Stop duelling him: farm under tower, or take a side lane's waves if a teammate with wave clear can hold mid.
more: Another death makes him strong enough to dive you. Every wave you collect quietly brings you back toward your next item.
A side lane is a longer lane with more room to farm, and he loses his kill target if he follows you there.
One shutdown assist in a later fight covers most of the gap, but only if you still have items when it comes.
check: Can anyone else hold the mid wave, and where has their jungler been showing?
breaks: Wrong if the side lane has no vision and their jungler is missing: under your mid tower is the safer place.
basis: pro:Behind in mid, go and farm a side

when: the enemy team has two or more dive champions and you are an immobile mage
asks: what do I buy against their dive
should I get Zhonya's early
they keep jumping on me
damage or defense second
say: Buy the armor stasis component early and finish it later; it keeps you alive now. Or keep building damage if they haven't reached you yet.
more: The component is cheap and already has the stasis. It turns their whole dive into a wait while your team arrives.
You don't need to finish the item straight away. If fights go well you can sit on it and build damage in the meantime.
Building pure damage looks better on paper, but a mage who dies first in every fight deals none of it.
check: Who on their team can reach you, and have they been ignoring you or going straight for you?
breaks: Wrong if their damage is mostly magic or they have no way onto you: go straight for damage.
basis: pro:Buy the stasis component early

when: you died in the last three minutes and the enemy has an assassin or a dive jungler
asks: I keep getting caught in the side lane
their assassin keeps killing me
how do I farm side safely
should I stop going to side lane
say: Farm side only with a ward behind you and a teammate in the nearby jungle, or take mid waves and let someone tankier go side.
more: An assassin who is behind comes back through exactly this: a carry alone in a long lane, again and again.
You don't have to give up the farm. You need to see him coming or have a second body close enough to turn it.
Swapping lanes with a tankier teammate fixes it too. He gets nothing from jumping on a bruiser.
check: Is there a ward on the path behind you, and do you know where their assassin is right now?
breaks: Wrong if you can see him on the other side of the map: then the wave is free, take it and leave.
basis: pro:Carries get picked in the long lane

when: baron or elder dragon is alive
asks: how do I check this bush
is it safe to walk here
do I face check
they might be in the brush
say: Throw a skillshot or a pet into the brush before you walk past, or wait for your tank to go first.
more: Late in the game one face-check is the baron. An ability costs a few seconds of cooldown and tells you just as much.
If it hits something, you already know where they are and you're still at full range.
With no ability to spare, walk behind the player they don't want to jump on.
check: Which brushes on your path have no ward, and how many enemies are missing?
breaks: Wrong if the ability you'd throw is the one you need to survive a dive: keep it and go around through warded ground.
basis: pro:Check the brush with an ability

when: your support is dead or has recalled
asks: my support died, do I stay
can I get this plate alone
should I keep pushing
support's gone, what now
say: Back off to your tower and farm what comes to you, or finish the plate only if you can see three of them elsewhere.
more: A carry alone and pushed up is the easiest play on the map for them. The kill you just got flips into a shutdown for them.
The plate is not gone if you leave it. The same wave advantage is there when your support walks back.
What you can't get back is the death timer and the wave that dies to their tower while you're grey.
check: How many enemies do you see on the map, and how long until your support is back?
breaks: Wrong if their bot lane is dead too and their jungler shows top: then take the plate, quickly.
basis: pro:A carry alone gives the lead back

when: after 14:00 and you have a wave-clearing or long-range marksman
asks: where do I go after laning
do I stay bot or go mid
which lane do I farm now
what's my job in mid game
say: Go mid and keep that wave pushed so your support and jungler can leave to ward, or take a side lane if mid is contested.
more: Mid is the short lane, so it's the safest one for you. A carry who clears it quickly frees two teammates to move first.
That is how vision gets set up before a dragon. It's rarely won by fighting for the river; it's won by the mid wave being gone.
You don't need to win a duel there. You only need the wave pushed before theirs is.
check: Is the mid wave pushing toward you or away, and who else on your team is standing mid?
breaks: Wrong if their mid laner or jungler can dive you there alone: then farm mid only with someone next to you.
basis: pro:The wave-clear carry holds mid

when: you have three finished items and more kills than deaths
asks: I'm fed, what do I buy next
more damage or defense
should I get a defensive item
what's my next item
say: Buy the item that answers how they kill you, like the crowd control cleanse or lifesteal; or more damage if nobody reaches you.
more: Once you already kill people fast enough, more damage changes little. What ends your lead is being locked down once.
A fed carry who can't be held in place has no answer. That's the difference between a lead and a won game.
Look at what killed you last, or what would. Buy against that one thing.
check: What is their most dangerous crowd control or burst, and did it land on you in the last fight?
breaks: Wrong if their front line is too tanky for you to get through: then the armor-shred item comes first.
basis: pro:The fed carry buys the answer

when: no dragon or baron spawns in the next minute, and a soul point dragon or baron is due within five minutes
asks: do I flash this
should I burn flash to live
caught, flash or die
is my flash worth it here
say: If nothing spawns right after, dying can cost less than losing Flash for the big fight; or Flash at once if you carry a bounty.
more: It sounds wrong, but they can't take anything with the kill when nothing is up. Flash stays down for minutes, right into the fight that matters.
A carry with Flash in the soul fight is far harder to kill than one who saved his life two minutes earlier.
The numbers change if you hold a shutdown. Then the gold you hand over is worth more than the cooldown.
check: What spawns next and when, and how many kills in a row do you have?
breaks: Wrong if they can take a tower, baron or dragon with you dead: then Flash, or your death is the objective.
basis: pro:Keep Flash for the fight that matters

when: you are Vayne against a marksman with better wave clear
asks: how do I play this lane as Vayne
he just pushes me in
do I fight him
I can't push against this
say: Take the duel whenever he's alone; Silver Bolts wins it. Or farm under tower and wait if his support is next to him.
more: You lose the wave and win the fight. He can shove all day, but he can't stand next to you for three hits.
Tumble out of his main skillshot and he has little left. With Final Hour the gap gets bigger.
Later this becomes a map problem for you. He will sit mid and clear, so you need fights to turn scrappy, or a side lane he must answer.
check: Where is his support, and has he used his main damage ability?
breaks: Wrong if their jungler is near or your own support is away: a two-on-one isn't a duel. Give the wave.
basis: pro:The duelist against the wave clearer

when: you are Sivir against a duelling marksman such as Vayne
asks: how do I lane against Vayne
she keeps all-inning me
do I fight her
what's my plan as Sivir here
say: Don't duel her; shove every wave with Ricochet and Boomerang Blade so she farms under tower. Or trade only with your support in front.
more: She beats you one on one early, and you beat her at minions for the whole game. Play the game you win.
Later, take the mid wave and keep it pushed. She can't clear it quickly, so her team is always second to the river.
Keep Spell Shield for the ability that starts her all-in, not for poke.
check: Is your support beside you, and how far up the lane is your wave?
breaks: Wrong if she has no support and you have your jungler: then the three-on-one is free. Take it.
basis: pro:The wave clearer against the duelist

when: you are Xayah and the enemy has two or more dive champions
asks: when do I use my ult
they keep diving me
how do I survive their assassins
do I ult the first guy
say: Walk away from the first diver and keep Featherstorm for the second one, or use it at once if the first hit would kill you.
more: Dive teams send someone in first to draw out your untargetable ultimate. The real damage arrives right after, while it's on cooldown.
If the first one can't kill you alone, answer him with your feet, your root and your support.
Featherstorm on the second diver leaves both of them in the middle of your team with nothing left.
check: Which of their divers is the fed one, and has he gone in yet?
breaks: Wrong if the first diver is the fed one and can kill you alone: use it on him and back out of the fight.
basis: pro:Don't answer the feint

when: you are Soraka
asks: how do we fight with Soraka
should we fight fast or slow
what's my job in fights
when is Soraka strong
say: Aim for long fights: let them poke, heal it back, then fight on full health bars. Or back off if they can one-shot someone.
more: Everything they deal that doesn't kill, you undo. A team that pokes into you for a minute ends up worse off than when it started.
Wish answers a big area ultimate. If it doesn't kill outright, the fight simply restarts in your favour.
Your weak point is you. If you die first, your team has no healing and a support who did nothing.
check: Who on their team can kill a carry in one rotation, and can any of them reach you?
breaks: Wrong if they have enough burst to delete your carry from full health: healing never happens. Play for picks and vision instead.
basis: pro:A healer wants the long fight

when: the enemy support is a healer such as Soraka
asks: how do we beat their Soraka
they just heal everything
who do I focus
do I need anti-heal
say: Kill the healer first or kill one target outright; poking them is wasted. And have two of you buy healing reduction.
more: Half-killing people does nothing against a healer. Either the target dies in one go, or the damage is healed back a moment later.
The healer is usually slow and fragile. Whoever on your team can reach the back line has her as the first job.
Healing reduction on two or three champions is cheap and cuts every fight short for them.
check: Where is their healer standing, and who on your team can reach her?
breaks: Wrong if she is unreachable behind two tanks: then stop taking long fights and trade objectives across the map.
basis: pro:Burst or anti-heal against a healer

when: you are Nocturne and you are level 6 or higher
asks: do I save my ult
when do I use Paranoia
ult for the gank or keep it for dragon
should I ult now
say: Use Paranoia whenever it's up on a carry without Flash, even just to burn summoners; or keep it if a dragon spawns within a minute.
more: You won't out-farm a faster-clearing jungler, so each ultimate has to buy something. A Flash taken is a kill at the next objective.
A Nocturne who holds it for the perfect moment casts it half as often. The game is over before the perfect moment comes.
It also removes their shared vision, so every cast lets your lanes step up for a few seconds as well.
check: Which carries have no Flash, and how long until the next dragon or herald?
breaks: Wrong if the target has a stasis item or a tank beside him and your team can't follow: you arrive alone. Pick someone else.
basis: pro:Press the ultimate more often

when: you play a dash champion and the enemy has Poppy or Cassiopeia
asks: how do I get onto them
I can't dash into their team
Poppy keeps stopping me
how do I play into Cassiopeia
say: Wait for Steadfast Presence or Miasma to be used before you dash in, or go for a target standing away from them.
more: Both abilities stop movement abilities. Dashing into them means you're stuck in the middle of their team.
They are also the answer their team is relying on. Once it's been used on someone else, the back line is open for a few seconds.
Walking in and dashing out afterwards works. So does picking the carry on the other side of the fight.
check: Has that ability just been used, and how close is its owner to your target?
breaks: Wrong if your team's engage is already in and they used it on him: go straight away, the window is short.
basis: pro:Wait out the anti-dash ability

when: you are an assassin and a teammate also dives
asks: when do I go in
do I go first
how do I get their carry
I keep dying when I jump in
say: Let your other diver go first and draw their defensive ult, then jump the same carry; or go first only if the carry's alone.
more: Carries keep one button for the first threat they see. Whoever goes second finds a target with nothing left.
The first diver doesn't have to commit. He goes in, forces the answer and walks out.
Come from a different side than he did. Their peel is all facing the first threat.
check: Has their carry used his defensive ultimate or stasis, and where is their peel standing?
breaks: Wrong if your team is losing the front line while you wait: go on whoever you can reach before the fight is over.
basis: pro:The second assassin gets the kill

when: your team is behind in kills and you are an assassin jungler with two finished items
asks: we're behind, what can I do
how do I get us back in the game
should I just farm
who do I go for
say: Go for the carry who farms a side lane alone, again and again, then take the tower there; or farm if they move as five.
more: Assassin items are cheap. You can be the strongest player in the game for a few minutes while your team is still behind.
The same isolated carry will give you the same kill until he stops going there. Each one is a shutdown and a tower.
Small pieces add up: a kill, a herald, their first tower. That's how a gap closes without winning a five-on-five.
check: Which enemy carry is alone in a side lane, and does he have Flash?
breaks: Wrong if they start walking as a group with a bodyguard: stop looking for him, and trade for camps and waves on the other side.
basis: pro:The assassin's cheap spike

when: the enemy team has two or more dive champions and your team has more range
asks: how do we fight their dive
where do I stand
they all jump on one person
how do we teamfight this
say: Spread out so one dive can't reach two of you, and shoot whoever jumps in; or fall back to a tower if they flank.
more: A dive team has to put everything on one target, which bunches all of them up in one place.
If your other carries are a little apart and still alive, that bunch is the best target you'll get all game.
So losing one player isn't losing the fight. Standing close enough to lose two is.
check: Where are your other two damage dealers standing, and who on their team is missing?
breaks: Wrong if they're much further ahead and one dive kills through your whole front line: don't take the fight in the open at all.
basis: pro:Spread out against a dive team

when: an objective spawns within a minute and the enemy has a hook champion such as Blitzcrank, Thresh, Nautilus or Pyke
asks: they're already at dragon, do we walk in
how do we contest this
they got there first
can we go into the river
say: Don't walk in second against a hook; push a side wave so they come out to you, or give it and take a tower.
more: Arriving second means walking through dark brush toward a champion whose whole job is pulling one of you out of it.
A wave crashing somewhere else makes them leave the dark to answer it. That gives you the river without the face-check.
Next time, the fix is half a minute earlier: be the team standing there first.
check: Which brushes on the way in are warded, and where was their hook champion last seen?
breaks: Wrong if you can see the hook champion on the map away from the pit: then walk in now, before he's back.
basis: pro:Never arrive second against a hook

when: the enemy has two or more big tanks and a dragon or baron is up
asks: do we fight in the pit
how do we fight their tanks
should we go in on them at dragon
where do we fight
say: Stay out of the pit and fight them in the open river where you can back up, or give it if they've already boxed you in.
more: Close quarters are a tank's best place. Every area effect hits all of you, and your carries have nowhere to step back to.
In open ground the same tanks have to walk at you through your damage. Most of what they do never reaches a second target.
If you must contest, hit whoever walks out first. Don't jump into the middle.
check: Are they inside the pit or outside it, and which exits are open behind you?
breaks: Wrong if their tanks have already used their ultimates: then the pit is safe to fight in for the next few seconds.
basis: pro:No brawls in the pit against tanks

when: a dragon or baron is up and there have been no kills in the last minute
asks: their tank used his ult, do we go
they wasted their ults, now what
do we fight again
is this our window
say: If their key ultimate is down and yours is up, force the next fight now; or wait and reset if you're not sure it was used.
more: An ultimate advantage is a real lead, but it's a short one. It's gone the moment theirs comes back.
Go at them within that time, on ground you choose. If your own ultimate misses, though, you're back to even.
So set it up first: a slow, a stun or a wall, then the big ultimate on top of it.
check: Did you see their engage or defensive ultimate used, and is yours ready?
breaks: Wrong if their damage dealers are far ahead in items: one missing ultimate doesn't make up for that. Take vision and wait.
basis: pro:Fight inside the ultimate window

when: after 14:00 and no ally has died in the last 30 seconds
asks: do I go back for him
should I help
my jungler got caught, do I go in
do we turn and fight
say: If he's already out, leave with him; don't spend your ult on a fight that's over. Or turn only if your whole team is there.
more: The rescue has already worked. Going back in gives them a second target who is closer and has fewer cooldowns.
Plenty of fights are lost this way: the first player escapes and the teammate who came to help is the one who dies.
Watching for it is enough. If they chase too far into your team, then you turn.
check: Is he out of their range, and how many of your team are close enough to fight?
breaks: Wrong if he's still locked down and your ultimate is what frees him: use it, that is what it's for.
basis: pro:Don't rescue someone who is already safe

when: your team just took an objective and you want to recall
asks: can I recall here
where do I back
is it safe to back now
we got the grubs, do I base
say: Walk out of the river to your tower or a brush you know is unwarded before you recall, or stay grouped until the team backs together.
more: Right after an objective is when the other team goes looking for someone. They want anything back for what they lost.
A recall in a spot they can see is an invitation, and worse if your Flash is down.
A few seconds walking to a safe spot is cheap next to a death and a shutdown just after you got ahead.
check: Is there an enemy ward near you, and is your Flash up?
breaks: Wrong if the whole enemy team is dead or seen far away: then recall where you stand and save the time.
basis: pro:Don't recall on their ward

when: the enemy took all three grubs and your team is ahead in towers or plates
asks: they got all the grubs, are we in trouble
is losing grubs bad
they have grubs, what now
did we mess up giving grubs
say: You're fine: grubs only pay at your towers, so keep them pinned on their own side; or contest the next dragon if lanes are even.
more: Grubs help break towers. A team that's being pushed into its own towers never gets to use them.
If your lanes took plates while they grouped for it, you were paid on the spot, in gold, and they hold a buff for later.
It turns against you only if you stop pushing and let them walk up to your towers.
check: Which of your lanes are pushed, and which of your outer towers are low?
breaks: Wrong if your side lanes are losing and stuck under tower: then the grubs will cost you those towers. Send help to the weakest lane.
basis: pro:Grubs only pay at towers

when: the enemy has three dragons and the next dragon spawns within a minute
asks: wave or dragon
do I catch this wave first
should I leave my lane for dragon
can I get this wave before the fight
say: Leave the wave and be at the dragon; a few minions are the price of this fight. Or stay only if your team's giving it.
more: On most dragons a pushed wave is worth showing up a bit late for. Not on this one: their soul changes every fight after it.
Four against five at that pit loses the soul and usually two or three players as well.
Push what you can early, then walk. If you're choosing at the last second, the answer is the dragon.
check: How long until the spawn, and is your team going to fight for it?
breaks: Wrong if your team has clearly decided to give it: then take the wave and a tower, don't stand between the two.
basis: pro:A wave is the entry fee for the soul fight

when: you are behind and the enemy team outscales yours
asks: do we stall or fight
we're behind, should we just farm
how do we come back
do we wait for late game
say: Stalling won't help when they scale better; pick one carrying a shutdown and force it. Or farm only if your own carry is one item away.
more: Waiting is a plan only for the team that gets stronger with time. If that's them, each quiet minute makes the gap bigger.
A shutdown is the fastest gold on the map. One clean pick on their richest player can buy a fight you can take.
Choose the target before you go: the one who is alone, or the one with no Flash.
check: Who on their team carries a bounty, and is he ever alone or without Flash?
breaks: Wrong if your team has the late-game carries: then stalling is correct. Clear waves and give what you can't hold.
basis: pro:Stalling only helps the scaling team

when: the enemy killed baron in the last two minutes and you are defending
asks: they have baron, how do we defend
how do we hold the base
do we fight them at the tower
what do we do against baron
say: Clear the waves from range and jump on whoever steps up alone; one pick runs their buff out. Or give the outer tower.
more: The buff has a timer. Each kill sends someone to base and takes a slice of it, and the siege waits while he walks back.
You don't need to win a five-on-five. You need them to be four for half a minute, twice.
What loses it is standing in front of the tower taking poke until someone is low enough to dive.
check: Which of them walks up first to hit the tower, and does he have Flash?
breaks: Wrong if they're pushing two lanes at once with nobody stepping forward: just clear waves and trade a tower for time.
basis: pro:A pick stalls the baron push

when: your team killed baron in the last minute
asks: we have baron, where do we push
how do we use baron
which lane first
do we group or split with baron
say: Wait until two waves arrive together, then push both lanes at once; or recall and spend first if you're holding gold.
more: One wave under a tower gets cleared. Two lanes arriving at the same moment force them to split, and one of the towers falls.
It takes a few seconds of lining up. That's time well spent with a buff that lasts minutes.
Don't send one player far ahead into the dark to hurry it. A pick on him is the only thing that stops the push.
check: Where are the three waves, and how much unspent gold does your team have?
breaks: Wrong if their wave clear is weak and they're short a player: skip the setup and take the inhibitor right now.
basis: pro:Line up two waves for the siege

when: three or more enemies are dead after 25:00
asks: can we end
do we go for the nexus
end or baron
we won the fight, what now
say: Go for the end only with a big wave and long death timers; otherwise take baron or the soul and end on the next push.
more: Without minions the towers shoot you, and one tank who is alive or back early can clear the wave and hold long enough.
A failed end attempt gives the game back: you're low, deep in their base, and they respawn together.
Baron first makes the next push a sure thing. It's slower, but it doesn't depend on a race.
check: How long are their death timers, how many minions are at their base, and who on their team is still alive?
breaks: Wrong if their inhibitors are already down and super minions are in the base: then go, the wave is already there.
basis: pro:Ending needs a wave, not only kills

when: an enemy inhibitor is down, elder dragon is up and you have Teleport
asks: they're doing elder, do I go
should I backdoor
tp to their base or the fight
can I end while they do elder
say: If all five are at elder and super minions are in their base, Teleport there and end; or join the fight if two can recall.
more: Five players at the dragon means nobody is home. Super minions plus one champion can finish towers very quickly.
They then have to choose: stop the dragon and recall, or finish it and lose the game.
Your team's job is to make leaving hard. A slow or a stun on whoever tries to recall is enough.
check: How many of them are visible at the dragon, are the nexus towers up, and is there a minion to Teleport to?
breaks: Wrong if both nexus towers are healthy and no minions are near: you won't finish in time. Teleport to the fight instead.
basis: pro:End through the open base during elder

when: your team is far ahead in kills and towers but has mostly melee or short-range champions
asks: we're so far ahead, why can't we end
how do we break their base
do we dive the inhibitor tower
what do we do with this lead
say: Don't dive their inner towers without baron; set up vision and make them come out for it. Or push a side wave with a duelist.
more: Short-range teams can't hit a defended tower safely. Every attempt is a dive, and a dive is what the losing team is hoping for.
Baron fixes that. The buffed minions take the tower so you don't have to stand under it.
Until it spawns, the lead is spent on vision around the pit and on denying their jungle, not on their base.
check: Is baron up or how long until it is, and how good is their wave clear?
breaks: Wrong if two or more of them are dead: then the tower isn't defended any more. Take it now.
basis: pro:A short-range lead needs baron to siege

when: after 20:00, you have two finished items and a soul point dragon or baron is next
asks: what do I buy third
should I get Guardian Angel
damage or a defensive item
what item before baron
say: Finish a revive or stasis item before the big objective; one extra life there is worth more than damage. Or buy damage if you're behind.
more: You are the player who has to stand in the pit and Smite. Whoever kills you first usually gets the objective.
An item that lets you survive the first burst means the Smite contest still has two junglers in it.
If their jungler has one and you don't, you're the easier one to remove. That's often the whole fight.
check: What does their jungler have, and how long until the objective spawns?
breaks: Wrong if you're so far behind that you die twice anyway: then build what helps your team's carry instead.
basis: pro:One extra life in the pit

when: your team is behind in towers
asks: where do I ward when we're behind
we have no vision
should I ward river
how do we get vision back
say: Put wards and control wards at your own jungle entrances first, or go to the river only with three teammates after a pushed wave.
more: When you're behind, the river belongs to them. A ward placed there alone lasts seconds and often costs the person placing it.
Wards at your own entrances show them coming. That's what keeps your carries alive on side waves.
The line moves forward again after you win something: a pick, a pushed mid wave, an enemy seen far away.
check: Which of your jungle entrances are dark, and where is their team showing?
breaks: Wrong if a soul point dragon or baron is about to spawn: then you need the river anyway. Go early and go together.
basis: pro:Ward your own jungle when behind

when: after 14:00 and your CS has barely risen in the last three minutes
asks: we're all mid, is that right
why am I not getting farm
should I leave mid
who catches the side waves
say: Someone has to catch the side waves; go if you're safe alone there, or stay mid only if a fight's about to start.
more: Five players in mid share one wave while two others die to towers. That loses gold every minute with nothing to show for it.
Grouping to catch someone works once. After the other team has seen it, they just clear mid and farm the sides.
The safe side is the one where their strongest duelist is not.
check: Which side wave is closest to your tower, and which enemies are showing mid?
breaks: Wrong if an objective spawns within half a minute: then stay, the wave is the price of being there.
basis: pro:Five in mid starves the team
